name: Portable Generator Set
tagline: An engine turning an alternator — a separate source that must never touch the supply network.
terminals: 230 V socket outlets on the control panel
12 V DC output on some sets
Changeover switch or interlocked breaker at the installation
parts: Engine — diesel or petrol, governed to hold 50 Hz
Alternator — brushless, with an AVR holding the voltage
Control panel with sockets, breakers and meters
safety: Back-feeding a generator into an installation that is still connected to the network can kill a linesman on the street, so a generator must be interlocked with the supply — a changeover switch or a mechanically interlocked breaker, never a lead plugged into a socket. It also needs its own earthing arrangement: a portable set is a separate source, not an extension of the building's earth.

points.label: Top cowling, muffler and fuel cap
points.detail: The silenced exhaust and the filler both live on top of a portable set. Exhaust gas and heat are why a generator runs outdoors or in a purpose-built enclosure with a through-wall flue — never in a garage or a hallway, and never just inside a doorway.

points.label: Engine
points.detail: The engine is governed to hold the speed that gives 50 Hz: 3,000 rpm for a two-pole alternator, 1,500 rpm for a four-pole. Frequency is a direct function of shaft speed, so a set that is hunting or sagging is an engine problem before it is an electrical one.

points.label: Alternator
points.detail: A brushless machine with a rotating exciter feeding the main rotor through a rectifier, so there are no brushes to wear. The AVR senses the output voltage and adjusts the excitation to hold it steady as the load changes — which is what stops the lights dipping when a motor starts.

points.label: Control panel and socket outlets
points.detail: Sockets, an output breaker, and usually a voltmeter and frequency meter. The breaker protects the alternator against overload; it does not make the set safe to connect to an installation, and the RCD on the panel only protects what is plugged directly into the set.

points.label: Base frame and anti-vibration mounts
points.detail: The set sits on rubber mounts so engine vibration is not transmitted into the frame or the floor. It also carries the earth stud: a portable generator used as a standalone source has no path back to the supply earth, so the frame is bonded to the local electrode rather than relying on the installation.

points.label: Earth stud
points.detail: Where the set feeds a fixed installation through a changeover switch, the earthing arrangement is decided at the design stage — TT with its own rod, or bonded into the existing system under the control of the changeover device. Getting this wrong leaves exposed metal with no fault path at all.

cutaway.alt: Cutaway of a portable generator set showing the engine cylinder and piston, the alternator stator and rotor, the AVR and the anti-vibration mounts

cutawayPoints.label: Engine
cutawayPoints.detail: The prime mover, governed to hold a fixed speed because the output frequency depends directly on it: 3000 rpm for 50 Hz on a two-pole machine. Everything electrical about a generator set is downstream of that governor — a hunting engine is a hunting frequency, and sensitive electronics will not thank you for it.

cutawayPoints.label: Piston and crank
cutawayPoints.detail: Turns the fuel into rotation. It is also why a generator is a load-following machine with a lag: when a motor starts, the engine has to pick up the torque, so the speed dips and the voltage and frequency dip with it before the governor catches up.

cutawayPoints.label: Alternator stator
cutawayPoints.detail: The stationary windings the output is taken from. On a brushless set there are two: the main stator that supplies the load and a smaller exciter stator whose output is rectified and fed to the rotor, which is how the field is created without brushes or slip rings to wear.

cutawayPoints.label: Alternator rotor
cutawayPoints.detail: The rotating field. Its excitation is what the AVR varies to hold the output voltage as the load changes — more excitation, more voltage. It is also the part that carries residual magnetism, and a set that has sat unused for a year sometimes has to be flashed to build a voltage at all.

cutawayPoints.label: AVR
cutawayPoints.detail: The automatic voltage regulator: it senses the output and adjusts the field current to hold the voltage steady. It is the difference between a generator you can run electronics on and one you cannot, and it is why a set with a failed AVR may still spin and still read full frequency with useless output.

cutawayPoints.label: Anti-vibration mounts
cutawayPoints.detail: Rubber mounts between the set and its frame. They keep the engine vibration out of the frame and the ground, and they are also part of why a portable generator must never be a substitute for an earthing arrangement — it is a floating source, and what you do with its earth depends on how it is connected, not on these mounts.
